chunks: Ali, from his father, from Hammad, from Aban ibn 'Uthman, raised it to one of the two (Imams) (peace be upon them), who said:
The meaning of 'separation between the two' is that they are not alone, and that there is a third person with them.

key_terms.يَخْلُوَانِ: they are alone / two being alone together

ai.seo_question: What does 'separation between the two' mean in the context of Ihram rituals?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the legal nuance of 'separation' (talfiq) in Ihram, interpreting it not as absolute isolation but as the presence of a third party to prevent total privacy. This distinction is crucial in Shia jurisprudence for determining the validity of marital intimacy during pilgrimage rituals, ensuring the act does not violate the sanctity of the state while remaining permissible under specific conditions.

en.hubeali:
Ali, from his father, from Hammad, from Aban Bin Usman, 
(It has been narrated) raising it to one of the two (5<sup>th</sup> or 6<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) having said:
‘The meaning of ‘effecting separation between the two)’, i.e.. They both should not be together without there happening to be a third person along with them’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali has narrated from his father from Hammad from Aban ibn ‘Uthman in a marfu‘ manner who has said the following: “One of the two Imam, (abu Ja’far or abu ‘Abd Allah), ‘Alayhim al-Salam, has said, ‘
The meaning of separating them is that they must not stay together without a third person being with them.’”
